clue.text: This is the wrong place literally

definitions.text: This is the wrong place literally

parts.words: This is the wrong place literally
parts.note: taken literally, a wrong is a crime and a place is a scene, so the spot where an offence happened is the wrong place

explanation.surface: Someone insists, quite literally, that they have come to the wrong spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrong place' reads as a mistake of location; 'literally' tells you to read 'wrong' as a noun, an offence, and 'place' as where it happened.
explanation.definitionFit: Detectives call the location where an offence was committed by this stock phrase.

clue.text: Ruler affirms they are independent countries

parts.note: a monarch is a sovereign, a ruler
to state something is to affirm it

explanation.surface: A monarch declares that some nations are self-governing.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-governing nations are termed this in international law.

clue.text: Write name in the list of another loner

indicators.note: another version of the word loner, a different arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: A recluse signs up for something, joining a register of solitary types.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' asks for another arrangement of LONER.
explanation.definitionFit: To register is to put your name down on a roll of members.

clue.text: Cast a spell can then transform

indicators.note: to transform the words can then is to rework their letters into a new shape

explanation.surface: A witch casts a spell and is then able to change something's form.
explanation.definitionFit: To bewitch someone is to put them under a magic spell.

clue.text: Stupidity even without Tom

parts.note: a common word for silly behaviour begins with the name Tom; drop that name and what remains still means silliness

explanation.surface: Someone remains silly even when their friend Tom is not around.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue treats Tom as a person who isn't there; really it is the first three letters of a longer word for silliness, which is still silliness without them.
explanation.definitionFit: Silly, clownish behaviour is daft nonsense, and that is what the shortened word means.

clue.text: Make the most economical use of a man

definitions.text: Make the most economical use of
definitions.meaning: to manage resources thriftily, as in conserving one's strength

explanation.surface: Advice to get the best value out of a fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means conserve thriftily; as a noun it is a wife's partner.

clue.text: Music room

definitions.meaning: the word used before music written for a small group of players
a room, especially a private or official one

explanation.surface: A room set aside for music.
explanation.definitionFit: Small-ensemble classical music carries this name, and the word also means a room or hall.

clue.text: Concentrated in the numbers I have

parts.note: tens are numbers
I have contracts to I've

explanation.surface: Someone describes how focused they are among their figures.
explanation.definitionFit: A concentrated effort is a thorough, highly focused one, as in intensive care.

clue.text: What to do with an anagram to keep in touch

definitions.text: What to do with an anagram
definitions.meaning: solving a jumble means swapping its characters about

explanation.surface: Advice on solving word puzzles and staying in contact.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally, swapping characters is how you solve a jumble; idiomatically, writing to one another keeps friends in contact.

clue.text: Truthful girl has many debts

parts.note: Vera is a girl's name
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, hence many
IOUs are written promises of debts

explanation.surface: A truthful young woman admits she owes a lot of money.
explanation.definitionFit: Veracity is honesty, so a veracious person speaks the truth.

clue.text: Salt but not in the cellar

definitions.text: Salt but not in the cellar

parts.words: Salt but not in the cellar
parts.note: ... salt is refined wit, and the room at the top of a house is the very opposite of the cellar

explanation.surface: Salt is found, but not in its cellar, the little dish that holds it.
explanation.walkthrough: A salt cellar holds salt; but read cellar as a basement, and the room at the top of the house is the opposite. 'Attic salt' is an old phrase for elegant wit, after Athens.
explanation.definitionFit: Attic salt means delicate wit, and the room under the roof is the opposite of a basement.

clue.text: Free film for the public to see

definitions.text: film for the public to see
definitions.meaning: a movie put out to cinemas, as in a new one

explanation.surface: A film that the public can watch without paying.
explanation.definitionFit: To liberate is to free, and a newly issued film is a new one in cinemas.

clue.text: Country introducing prohibition inter alia

indicators.note: inter is Latin for between or among, so one piece goes among the letters of the next word

parts.note: a ban is a prohibition

explanation.surface: A nation that brings in a prohibition among other things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inter alia' reads as the Latin phrase for 'among other things'; split it, and 'inter' (Latin for among) is the container signal while 'alia' is the fodder. 'introducing' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: A Balkan state on the Adriatic coast.

clue.text: Manage to compete in a race

definitions.meaning: to manage a business or project
to take part in a race as a runner or candidate

explanation.surface: Someone manages to take part in a race.
explanation.definitionFit: To operate a firm is to manage it, and to stand or sprint in a contest is to compete.

clue.text: Pity Len performed so unskilfully

indicators.note: the words Pity Len, performed, are acted out in a different order

explanation.surface: Sympathy for Len, who gave a clumsy performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something clumsily is doing it without aptitude.

clue.text: Is he always on the look-out

definitions.text: Is he always on the look-out

parts.words: Is he always on the look-out
parts.note: look-out read as looking outwards: someone whose attention turns outward to other people rather than inward

explanation.surface: Asks whether a sentry is permanently on watch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the look-out' suggests a watchman; read it as looking outwards, the outgoing personality type opposite the introvert.
explanation.definitionFit: Jung's term for an outgoing personality focused on the outer world.

clue.text: Some pleasant grassland

indicators.note: some of the word pleasant supplies a short run of its letters

explanation.surface: A pleasant bit of grassland.
explanation.definitionFit: A poetic word for a meadow.

clue.text: It is risky to be embracing a learner, love

indicators.note: embracing means holding something in its arms, so one word goes around the letter

parts.note: something daring is bold and risky
L stands for learner, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: It's dangerous to hug a novice, my love.
explanation.definitionFit: A term of endearment, like sweetheart.

clue.text: An attempt in the past

parts.note: to have a go is to make an attempt

explanation.surface: A try made some time before.
explanation.definitionFit: Used after a span, as in years before now.

clue.text: An idiot being the obvious choice

definitions.meaning: an old word for someone born simple-minded
a person ideally suited, as in a born leader

explanation.surface: A fool turns out to be the clear pick.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaically a simpleton; today someone perfectly suited to a role.

clue.text: Again write letters in the correct order about a magic formula

definitions.text: Again write letters in the correct order

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a spell is a magic formula

explanation.surface: A wizard rewrites the letters of an incantation properly.
explanation.definitionFit: Spelling a word a second time, setting its characters out properly.

clue.text: Doctor in goal strangely going round the bend with pain

indicators.note: in tells us the doctor and bend letters sit inside the jumbled word
going round means the jumbled letters encircle the other pieces in this clue
the word goal, strangely altered, has its letters rearranged

parts.note: a U-bend, a bend shaped like the letter U
MB is a medical degree, Bachelor of Medicine, hence a doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor in goal is behaving so oddly that he is driven mad by pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round the bend' looks like the idiom for going mad, but it is split: 'going round' is a container signal and a U-bend gives U. 'strangely' turns the fodder into LAGO, which goes round UMB.
explanation.definitionFit: A painful ache in the lower back.

clue.text: Study manufacture of lace or hide

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart

indicators.note: the manufacture of a thing is its making, so the word lace is reworked

explanation.surface: A survey of how lace or leather hides are made.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep something out of sight.

clue.text: Carrying capacity of a vehicle?

parts.note: the amount a motor will hold, taken literally as its full burden

explanation.surface: Asks how much a vehicle can carry.
explanation.definitionFit: The quantity that fills an automobile or railway truck.

clue.text: Moan about Richard endlessly wandering

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so moan is rearranged
endlessly means the final letter is cut off the short name

parts.note: Dick is short for Richard

explanation.surface: Someone complains about Richard drifting about without end.
explanation.definitionFit: Nomads roam from place to place rather than settling.

clue.text: Composer thus leaving the country

indicators.note: leaving means that the word for thus departs from the name

parts.note: John Philip Sousa, the American march composer
so means thus

explanation.surface: A musician departs his homeland in this way.
explanation.definitionFit: The United States, a nation.

clue.text: Hurried in, most upset about a lintel

indicators.note: in tells us the verb for hurried goes inside the jumbled letters
upset means knocked over, so the word most is rearranged

parts.note: ran means hurried

explanation.surface: Someone rushed in, very upset about a beam over the door.
explanation.definitionFit: A crosspiece above a door or window, like a lintel.

clue.text: Back to ruin some of the defence

indicators.note: back means the word for ruin is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: to mar is to ruin
a part is some of a thing

explanation.surface: Retreat to wreck part of the fortification.
explanation.definitionFit: A defensive embankment or wall around a fort.

clue.text: A Wren working on an agricultural machine

indicators.note: working on the letters of A Wren puts them into a new order

explanation.surface: A naval servicewoman operates farm equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that removes the bristly beards from barley.

clue.text: Egotist's subject

parts.note: split into two words, it is the person a self-centred talker always discusses: himself

explanation.surface: What a self-centred person likes to talk about.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, it is what an egotist talks about: 'the me'.
explanation.definitionFit: A topic or subject of discussion, which for a self-obsessed person is always themselves.

clue.text: Legal non-payment of tax?

parts.note: the lawful way of dodging the taxman, as opposed to the criminal evasion

explanation.surface: Asks about lawfully not paying tax.
explanation.definitionFit: Tax avoidance is lawful minimising of liability, unlike evasion.

clue.text: Check the sporting record books to put an end to long standing grudges

definitions.meaning: taken literally, to resolve results of past matches

definitions.text: put an end to long standing grudges
definitions.meaning: to take revenge for past wrongs

explanation.surface: A fan checks old results to finally end long feuds.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally, to resolve past results; idiomatically, to get even for old injuries.
